# Copper stalls on Greek tragedy 



- Strong fluctuations in the value of the US dollar compared to other currencies continue to affect the copper price, which had retreated from $8,000/t in early April to around $7,700/t from 16<sup>th</sup> to 27<sup>th</sup> April, but then fell to $7,400/t at the time of writing. 



- Positive recovery prospects have so far provided support for prices from a fundamental perspective, but macroeconomic events are driving the volatility and weighing on copper prices. 



- Changes in Chinese scrap import regulations may reduce scrap supply from 1<sup>st</sup> June and therefore may lead to potentially higher cathode demand in China.  However, it is an open question whether this will translate into higher refined imports.  Currently, SHFE warehouse stocks are at record levels and globally production continues to see few disruptions.

# Market driven more by macro than fundamentals 

On 6<sup>th</sup> April the official LME copper cash price reached a new high for the year of $7,951/t and the 3-month official copper price hit $7,971/t, with the 3-month copper price surpassing the $8,000/t barrier during that trading session.  Howe

ver, on 28th April the LME copper 3-month price retreated to below $7,400/t, having held above $7,800/t for two weeks and traded in a $7,600-$7,700/t range for another week after touching $8,000/t. Prices reached the recent highs due to the combination of a reduction in stocks in LME warehouses and, a temporary weakening in the value of the US dollar against other currencies. The sensitivity of the commodities and financial markets to every piece of economic news had also contributed to the volatility and higher prices, with the decline on 28th April sparked by the downgrading of Spanish debt and a revival of concerns about sovereign defaults in euro countries. Last year, copper prices showed a high correlation with the US dollar. This year that correlation has been Data: LME receding although both (copper prices and the value of the US dollar) are still following similar patterns. There are two major forces boosting the value of the US dollar (and therefore weighing on the copper price). Firstly, the US dollar is considered a safe haven in times of economic uncertainty and the sovereign debt risks in the euro area have therefore boosted the value of the dollar. Secondly, the US is exhibiting some signs of economic recovery that is also benefiting sentiment about the value of the dollar. From a fundamental perspective, market participants have been expecting consumption to continue to recover, with supply slow to react. Arguably, the lack of news that would contradict those expectations has been supporting the bullish views on copper prices. Macroeconomic events – as they affect refined copper consumption – have joined the dollar as an explanation of copper price fluctuations in recent weeks. For example, on 2nd April the US Labor Department announced that nonfarm employment increased by 162,000 in March and on 23rd April US data shown a 26.9% rise in new home sales in March (a record increase), although the absolute value was still 75% lower than the pre-crisis peak. Both pieces of news were taken as an indication of a recovering US economy and thus a potential increase in copper consumption, to which copper prices reacted positively. Financial sector reform is also back on the political agenda in the US and elsewhere. How these reforms will affect the commodity markets is still unclear. One thing is certain however: exchange rates will remain volatile and drive volatility in copper prices. Financial crises are usually followed by sovereign defaults.

So, while we expect more ructions in international bond markets, whether this translates into a resumption of wider financial market stress is an unknown quantity at the moment.  As the debt downgrades show, the most likely sovereign default at the moment is in the Euro area.  The rescue plan for Greece as initially agreed by leaders of the Eurozone has been estimated to be €45B and would require the assistance of the IMF.  However, the Euro countries have had difficulties agreeing the plan and it now also appears that Greece will require more funds. By the end of April, the rating agency Standard & Poors was the first agency to downgrade Greece‟s debt to “junk” status.  Spanish and Portuguese credit ratings have also been downgraded, though neither to “junk” status yet.

Elsewhere, China has introduced new real estate policies aiming to rein in a real estate bubble that has formed. Among a range of measures it has lifted the deposit on second homes.  This measure should curb high value construction and potentially reduce construction activity overall.  In addition, the government‟s announcement of a possible RMB appreciation has raised concern among copper industry participants, particularly those with export businesses whose margins would be squeezed by lower export earnings in RMB-terms or a loss of market share due to having to raise prices.  However, the effect of the revaluation would not necessarily lead to significantly lower cathode prices for Chinese fabricators, as LME prices would be bid up to reflect the changes in the relative value of the US dollar.  In fact, the RMB revaluation could be taken by investors as a vote of confidence by the Chinese government in the strength of the economy and therefore demand for commodities, which could cause even higher levels of investor activity in commodity markets, including copper. 

### **Premiums down in China, steady in Europe and the US but with little business** 

In China copper cathode premiums have declined rapidly in April.   however, the extent to how much the premiums have fallen is not very clear.  Most deals were closing at $80/t, but some were already down to $50/t towards the end of April.  The main reason for the decline in premiums is the closure of the favourable SHFE/LME arbitrage window.  Market participants confirm that there is enough copper supply in China, given the high level of imports over the last couple of months combined with rising domestic refined copper production. 

In the US, despite positive news reports about the economy, indicators of the strength of the copper consumption recovery in the US are mixed.  Improvements are evident in most of the brass mills sectors, except for copper tube for plumbing and air conditioning, where there is no sign of a real recovery yet.  In this regard, the US data showing new home sales rising at a record rate may

turn out to herald an upturn in this segment but there are no signs yet in the construction sector. Improvements in wirerod production in March may be either temporary or driven by the end of a very cold winter. A scarcity of trucks has increased freight rates and we understand that premiums are now slightly up from March to 4.0-5.0¢/lb. Participants in the market say that the higher freights costs are being passed on to consumers leaving the portion of the premium attributable to copper unchanged. In Europe, a visible y-o-y upturn in the major economies appeared in Q1 2010. This was mainly due to a recovery in exports (supported by the weakened euro) and restocking rather than a significant improvement in real domestic demand, given that refined consumption was growing faster than semis production. Unchanged premiums and limited spot business reflect this subdued underlying demand. ### **Chinese demand growth moderating…** Chinese consumption of copper remains strong but, as mentioned in the April Monitor, growth is expected to slow from the high rates seen in 2009 and into Q1 2010. In particular, the government‟s efforts to rein in the economy are expected to bear fruit and lead to economic growth slowing from Q1‟s 11.9% y-o-y rate. In addition, we expect to see the benefit to refined copper consumption again this year from the scarcity of available scrap but at a lower level of 100,000-150,000t vs. 400,000-500,000t in 2009. There is a risk that scrap imports could be hit by the change in customs regulations, which could lead to higher imports of copper cathodes than the 2.3Mt we forecast for this year. The Chinese government has released two major new regulations on scrap imports. The first states that, from 1st April 2010 onwards, importers are required to provide grades of metal scrap content on customs documents, based on specifications in the international market. The second regulation will be effective from 1st June 2010 and states that mixed scrap metal in containers will no longer be allowed and will have to be segregated by type. The focus of this regulation is on shipment categorisation and port control. a result.  To what extent this will affect refined supply in China is still open to debate.  Meanwhile, scrap discounts have widened in the US, where traders report that Chinese buying activity has slackened, which may be a consequence of either the improved scrap availability in China or may be the first signs of the impact of the scrap rule changes.  However, as Chinese regulatory changes are not always implemented fully, it is too early to say what will actually happen, so this remains a point to watch and we are tracking developments closely. 

### **…and North East Asia recovers to 2008 levels** 

North East Asian (Japan, Korea and Taiwan) copper **0** consumption has recovered to pre-crisis levels.  Production of copper semis and therefore demand for refined copper has recovered to the levels recorded in 2008.  The bounce back Data: CRU, MOEA, KOSIS has been fairly uniform across the three countries, although Japanese output had begun declining in mid-2008 and the recovery has only been to H2 2008 levels of around 70,000t/m rather than the 85,000t/m recorded from 2001 through to July 2008.  In fact, the impact of the downturn looks like a repeat of the last recession, when Japanese semis production fell from almost 100,000t/m in 2000 to 85,000t/m in subsequent years.  Semis production in all three has benefited from domestic stimulus efforts, but also from the increase in Chinese demand for copper semis.  China is not self-sufficient in semis capacity, so any increase in demand leads to higher imports, most of which comes from neighbouring countries.  As long as the macro picture remains supportive, the recovery in North East Asia appears sustainable. 

### **Stocks building up in China** 

Total stocks at exchange warehouse have been moving sideways since March.  However, there has not been a consistent trend across regions.  In the US (LME and Comex) warehouse stocks have been steady at 420,000430,000t since 12<sup>th</sup> February because of the convenience of storage (availability and favourable location i.e. close to South America) and expectations that US demand will recover before Europe.  In the US, the high level of exchange stocks means there is little pressure for consumers to book in material.  In Europe, stock levels are much lower and declined to under 70,000t, as copper cathode was shifted from LME warehouses to China as a result of the positive SHFE/LME arbitrage (mid-December 2009 through early March 2010). 

In China, stocks at SHFE warehouses rose to a record high of 187,907t on 22<sup>nd</sup> April.   The favourable SHFE/LME price arbitrage and the growth in consumption had encouraged imports to China, with March imports of copper cathode up at 337,125t, their highest level in the last ten months.  It is likely that some of the imports were delivered into SHFE warehouses. Wo|rld Adju|sted produ|ction incl|udes| © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 7 of 12 Copper Monitor May 2010 www.crumonitor.com # Consumption trends: ## **Wire and cable markets looking fairly solid…** Demand for copper wire from the wire and cable industry has exhibited some encouraging recovery signs so far, a finding which was supported by the generally optimistic sentiment demonstrated by the industry during CRU‟s attendance at the Wire 2010 trade show in Dusseldorf this month. However, European and North American industry sources were cautious to admit that the worst is definitely behind them. Traditional markets, such as commercial and residential building wire in the US, remain weak and are not yet showing signs of recovery. The latest high new home sales figures cannot yet be extrapolated into an upward trend. It will be interesting to ta

ke the pulse of the global industry at the CRU‟s 4<sup>th</sup> World Wire and Cable Conference in Gothenburg on 2-4 June. 

As in all copper products, the recovery in wire demand from the collapse in late 2008 and early 2009 is „Asia-centric‟, primarily driven by China and its trade partners in North East Asia.  As Chinese fabricating capacity approaches self-sufficient levels, Chinese fabricators are beginning to challenge suppliers from other parts of the world that were characterised until recently as „low cost‟ regions, primarily targeting to serve mature North American and European markets.  Thus, cost pressures remain and machinery and equipment for wire production and processing was the most well attended part of the show.  That was followed by materials, special wires and cable, test technology, measurement, control and regulation technologies as well as tools for process engineering. 



Equipment manufacturers report that there is strong customer interest in new equipment.  Not surprisingly, Chinese fabricators lead the way due to their aggressive capacity expansion plans, and generally are commencing production without delays.  Indian fabricators are also showing interest in additional production equipment.  However, compared with the Chinese, they are much slower to implement their business plans. 

The need to make products less environmentally demanding was addressed by leading participants.  Wire and cable manufacturers are determined to reduce their footprint.  To achieve this, the entire wire and cable supply chain has invested in innovative and market-orientated research and development programmes.  Innovations include more efficient production systems that require less energy, „greener‟ materials, such as Dow‟s bio PVC plasticisers that come from plants instead of fossil fuels and more effective logistical solutions. 

With LME copper prices hovering around US$8,000/t during the trade show, material cost was a major issue.  As a result, despite the signs of recovery, industry participants are reluctant to restock so as to not miss out on a price correction.  Apart from the high price levels, market participants expressed their

s|| © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 9 of 12 Copper Monitor May 2010 www.crumonitor.com # Industry News ## **Production** - On 31st March 2010 it was reported that Australia‟s Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) had approved the sale of **Cape Lambert** ‟s **Lady Annie** copper mine in Australia to Hong Kong-based **China Sci-Tech Holdings** for A$135M (~US$125M). The company has said it plans to restart Lady Annie in December. Lady Annie was put on care and maintenance in February 2009, and produced 16,000t of EW copper cathode in its last full production year in 2008. - It was announced on 31st March that a strike at the **Cerro Verde** copper-molybdenum mine in Peru had been averted. According to reports, the Ministry of Labour‟s Regional Director for Arequipa had declared the strike to be illegal, and discussions between the union and management will be held during April and May to try and resolve the issues. It is believed that miners were demanding a larger share of the profits. Cerro Verde is expected to produce 221,000t of copper-in-concentrate and 82,000t of EW copper cathodes in 2010. - A strike at the **Ok Tedi** copper-gold mine in Papua New Guinea by around half of the full time employees of **Ok Tedi Mining Ltd** ( **OTML** ) began on 1st April. Since the strike was not sanctioned by the union executive it was declared illegal by the government and the company sent a final letter on 14th April to employees warning that termination proceedings would be the next step if work did not resume. On 16th April, an agreement was reached and work resumed on 17th April, with a total production loss of around 5,000t of contained copper-in-concentrate. OTML reported that the company was able to perform some maintenance tasks during the stoppage, and hope to be able to replace some of the lost tonnage throughout the year. Prior to the strike, Ok Tedi had been expected to produce around 161,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2010. - It was announced on 12th April that **China Nonferrous Metal Mining** ( **CNMC** ) plans to invest US$6

00M in Zambian copper operations over the next two years. Around half of the money is to be invested in the **Luanshya Copper Mines’ Mulyashi** mining project, which CNMC expects to be able to commission in 2012, and the rest of the money is to be invested in various Zambian projects, including the expansion of the **Chambishi** copper smelter. CNMC acquired 80% of Luanshya Copper Mines for US$50M in June 2009, and restarted its sole mining operation, **Baluba** , in December 2009 after it had been placed on care and maintenance in December 2008. Baluba produced around 23,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2008. 



- On 20<sup>th</sup> April it was reported that the workers union at **Neves Corvo** underground copper-zinc mine in Portugal had notified the operator, **Lundin Mining** , of their intentions to hold a strike between 5<sup>th</sup> May and 12<sup>th</sup> May. Employees had held two hour strikes at the beginning of each shift between February and April. Neves Corvo is expected to produce 84,000t of copper-in-concentrates in 2010. 



- It was announced on 20<sup>th</sup> April that Diego Hernandez, currently president of **BHP Billiton** ‟s base metals division, has been appointed the new CEO of **Codelco** , the state copper mining company of Chile. He will begin in his new position on 19<sup>th</sup> May. 



- The latest developments in the long-running strike at Mexico‟s **Cananea** mine have been reported in statements from union representatives that any attempts by the Mexican government to dislodge them would result in the destruction of the mine by the workers using explosives. A Mexican court ruled in

- **Kazakhmys** announced on 26<sup>th</sup> April the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with **Jinchuan Group** of China to form a joint venture to develop Kazakhmys‟ Aktogay project in Kazakhstan. Jinchuan is to acquire a 49% stake in Aktogay for US$120M, and following the completion of the deal a feasibility study will begin. The project, estimated to cost between US$1.5B and US$2B to bring onstream, is expected to produce 100,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate and have a mine life of around 40 years. 

## **Exploration and Development** 





- On 8<sup>th</sup> April, **Sagittarius Mines Inc** (SMI), t

he operator of the **Tampakan** copper-gold project in the Philippines, delivered the completed project feasibility study to the **Government of the Philippines** for review. This delivery, ahead of the deadline of 16<sup>th</sup> April, fulfils one of the conditions of **Zijin Mining Group** ‟s offer of A$1.28 per share in its **Indophil Resources** takeover bid. Indophil Resources‟ main asset is a 37.5% stake in the Tampakan project, with Xstrata holding the majority 62.5% direct stake. CRU believes the Tampakan project could possibly start production by 2016 and reach 330,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate when operating at full capacity. 

- On 20th April, it was announced that work on **Southern Copper Corporation** ‟s **Tia Maria** project in Peru will halt for three months as a re-evaluation of the environmental impact takes place. This follows the decision by the Peruvian government to cancel a public meeting days earlier intended to outline the environmental impact of the project in southern Peru, after members of the local community blocked the Pan American highway - a key transport route - in protest over the project. Locals are said to be concerned over the potential loss of water supplies in the area and used similar tactics to prevent an earlier scheduled meeting in February. The project requires an investment of around US$1B and is expected to produce 120,000t/y of EW cathode at full production. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 





- **Dundee Precious Metals** announced on 25<sup>th</sup> March 2010 the completion of its previously announced transaction with **Weatherly International** for the purchase of Weatherly‟s Namibian **Tsumeb** smelter assets and related business including all land, plant and other assets used by or in connection with or which benefit or pertain to Weatherly‟s smelter business.  This follows Dundee‟s suspension of plans to build a copper and gold metals processing facility near its **Chelopech** copper-gold mine in Bulgaria.  Tsumeb already processes Chelopech concentrate, together with other material and produced 20,000t blister copper in 2009. 

- It was reported on 6<sup>th</sup> April that **Pan Pacific Copper** ( **PPC** ), a Japanese joint venture between **Nippon Mining & Metals Co** and **Mitsui Mining & Smelting Co** , plans to reduce refined copper output by 1.6% y-o-y in the first half of the next fiscal year, which runs from April to September. This reduction amounts to 4,700t of refined copper, bringing production down to 291,600t of copper for the period.

## **Consumption** 







- Japan‟s output of copper and copper-alloy fabricated products, including sheets and tubes, more than doubled in March to 76,060t (from 34,512t a year ago), preliminary data from the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** showed on 27<sup>th</sup> April.  This is the fifth straight monthly increase and the highest level since October 2008.  Output for the fiscal year ended 31<sup>st</sup> March was 754,014t, down by 6%. 

- **Poongsan Corporation** raised its sales targets, backed by strong Chinese demand.  The company is expecting to sell some 210,000t of copper and alloy semis in 2010, compared to an earlier forecast of 205,000t.  In addition, the company is expanding capacity in sheet and strip products used in electronics.  It was reported that sheet and strip capacity will increase by 22%, with the capacity to be on stream by 2012. 

- French cable maker **Nexans** released financial data, which confirmed that after four quarters of decline in 2009, sales in Q1 2010 stabilised.  In particular, Europe and North America stopped falling, while the MERA area (Middle East, Russia and Africa) area saw a 10% rise.  Special cables for industry and LAN cables rose but building remains weak and poor weather affected LV and MV energy infrastructure.  Restructuring has cut fixed costs by 6% from a year ago, and an upturn in sales is expected in Q2 2010.
